findings.problem: JobWorkflow exposes public primitive fields (String status, bool flags) allowing any combination of values including impossible states (e.g., status="sent" with is_sent=false, or is_validated=false with status="sent").
findings.failure_mode: Consumer code and internal methods can construct and transition to logically inconsistent states. A job can be marked 'sent' without being validated, or have conflicting flag values.
findings.fix: Replace pub primitive fields with a private struct and a fallible constructor. Replace status: String and is_validated/is_sent bools with a typed JobState enum that encodes the lifecycle (e.g., Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }).

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are boolean lifecycle flags that must be replaced with enums or typestates per the functional-core-performance reference.
findings.failure_mode: Boolean flags do not encode valid transitions. Code cannot enforce that validation must precede sending, and callers cannot pattern-match on lifecycle state.
findings.fix: Replace is_validated and is_sent with a single JobState enum: enum JobState { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }

findings.problem: status: String is a primitive type for a domain concept. mark_sent sets it to hardcoded "sent".to_string() which is not compile-time enforced.
findings.failure_mode: Any string value can be assigned to status. A typo or wrong string literal silently creates an invalid state. No compile-time guarantee that status reflects actual lifecycle.
findings.fix: Replace with a JobState enum so the lifecycle is encoded in the type system. Remove status field entirely.

findings.problem: mark_sent transitions any job to sent state without checking is_validated. A job can be marked sent without ever being validated.
findings.failure_mode: Business invariant violation: unvalidated jobs reach 'sent' state. No error path or guard exists.
findings.fix: Change mark_sent to accept a ValidatedJobWorkflow typestate or return Result<JobWorkflow, JobError>. Only accept jobs that are in a validated state. Use a typestate pattern: fn mark_sent(validated: ValidatedJobWorkflow) -> Result<JobWorkflow, MarkSentError>.

findings.problem: mark_sent sets is_sent = true and status = "sent" but never populates sent_at_epoch_ms, leaving it as the caller's pre-existing value (possibly None).
findings.failure_mode: Sent jobs may have no timestamp, making audit trails and SLA tracking impossible. Downstream code reading sent_at_epoch_ms may get None for an ostensibly 'sent' job.
findings.fix: Include sent_at_epoch_ms as a field of the Sent variant in the JobState enum, set it in the mark_sent transition (accepting a u64 or a clock abstraction from the imperative shell).

findings.problem: JobWorkflow is a public struct with no domain methods. The single function mark_sent takes the struct by value and mutates it, mixing core data with action logic. No separation of pure core and imperative shell.
findings.failure_mode: Cannot independently test the transition logic. Clock/timestamp concerns are not isolated to a shell layer. Adding new transitions (cancel, retry) would require modifying the same mutable function.
findings.fix: Define pure transition functions (mark_sent, validate, cancel) that take immutable input and return Result<NewJobWorkflow, TransitionError>. Provide a builder or factory in the shell layer for I/O and clock access.

findings.problem: No tests directory or test modules exist. The crate has zero behavioral coverage for JobWorkflow transitions.
findings.failure_mode: No evidence that transitions are correct, that illegal states are rejected, or that mark_sent gates on validation. Any change breaks behavior with no signal.
findings.fix: Add tests directory with tests covering: successful Pending->Sent transition, rejection of Validated->Sent when job is actually Pending, sent_at_epoch_ms is set on transition, and all typestate transitions compile only when valid.

findings.problem: No benchmarks exist. While this crate is small, performance claims or throughput requirements cannot be validated without benchmarking.
findings.failure_mode: If this crate becomes a hot path, performance regressions go undetected.
findings.fix: Add a benches/ directory with a benchmark for mark_sent and any hot-path transitions when performance requirements exist.

findings.problem: mark_sent uses "sent".to_string() allocating a new String for status every call. The struct itself allocates id: String on construction.
findings.failure_mode: Every mark_sent call allocates a new String. For high-throughput scenarios this is unnecessary allocation. id: String could be a newtyped JobId.
findings.fix: Replace status String with JobState enum (zero-allocation). Replace id: String with a newtyped JobId(String or bytes) that encapsulates validation at construction.

findings.problem: No dev-dependencies, benches, or test configuration in Cargo.toml.
findings.failure_mode: Cannot run cargo test, cargo bench, or cargo clippy as part of verification.
findings.fix: Add [[test]] and [[bench]] sections to Cargo.toml as needed, and ensure clippy is runnable.

residual_risk: Static review only. The crate is fundamentally broken: it cannot enforce domain invariants, allows any illegal state combination, and has zero tests. A complete refactor to typed domain errors, enums/typestates, and typestates is required before any production use. No commands were run.
